name: Isolated Gastric Duplication

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic structure with a smooth muscle coat contiguous with the stomach wall
Inner lining of the cyst composed of gastric mucosa
Identification of cystic lesion adjacent to the stomach on imaging studies (ultrasound, CT, MRI)
No communication between the cyst and the gastric lumen

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cystic structure with smooth muscle coat contiguous with stomach wall, gastric mucosal lining, and imaging identification of cystic lesion adjacent to stomach
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed postoperatively by histopathology.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically detected in infants or young children
searchTerms: cystic mass in upper stomach area

pathognomonic.notes: Vomiting and feeding intolerance due to mass effect
searchTerms: vomiting and fullness from gastric obstruction

common.notes: Due to partial gastric outlet obstruction

occasional.notes: Due to ulceration of ectopic gastric mucosa

searchTerms: low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia due to chronic blood loss

occasional.notes: If duplication cyst compresses pancreatic duct

occasional.symptomName: Infection or abscess formation within cyst

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to large cystic mass effect
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to mass effect
difficulty breathing caused by cyst pressure

laboratory: Anemia due to chronic gastrointestinal bleeding
Elevated inflammatory markers if cyst infected
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic lesion adjacent to stomach
CT or MRI demonstrating well-defined cystic mass with smooth muscle wall
No communication with gastric lumen on contrast studies
other: Histopathology confirming gastric mucosal lining and smooth muscle coat

distinguishingFeatures: Location related to pancreas rather than stomach
Lack of gastric mucosal lining on histology
Typical onset in infants with projectile vomiting
Different clinical presentation depending on site

redFlags: Signs of gastrointestinal bleeding (hematemesis or melena)
Signs of infection or sepsis (fever, elevated inflammatory markers)
references: Holcomb GW 3rd, Gheissari A, O’Neill JA Jr, Shorter NA, Bishop HC. Surgical management of alimentary tract duplications. Ann Surg. 1989;209(2):167-174.
Puligandla PS, Nguyen LT, St-Vil D, et al. Gastrointestinal duplications. J Pediatr Surg. 2003;38(5):740-744.
